title: Flatness is equivalent upstairs, on the support and on the finite cover, in the elementary devissage
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the flatness companion of the finite presentation comparison: it equates flatness of F near x, of G near z' and of pi_*G near y' over the base, and then repeats the comparison at the three local rings (statement lines 691-702). What is non-formal is that the etale up-and-down lemma is used to move between flatness over S and over S' while the remaining comparisons are made through the affine global sections Gamma(X', g^*F) = Gamma(Z', G) = Gamma(Y', pi_*G), so that the module-theoretic statement about pi_*G is reduced to one about G on a finite cover (proof lines 718-730). In the local-ring chain the corresponding identification of g^*F_{x'}, G_{z'} and pi_*G_{y'} as O_{S',s'}-modules is what allows a single descent along the faithfully flat map gamma to settle all three statements at once (proof lines 749-759). Both chains are short and use only quoted inputs, which places the claim at H2.
